```release-note
Currently, NodeAdded QueueingHint could not always be called because of the internal feature called preCheck.
It's definitely not something expected for plugin developers,
and we're trying to eventually remove preCheck completely to fix this.
Until then we'll register UpdateNodeTaint event for plugins that have NodeAdded event, but don't have UpdateNodeTaint event.
It'd result in a bad impact on the requeuing efficiency though, a lot better than some Pods being stuck in the
unschedulable pod pool.
```

@alculquicondor 

This change should be applied no matter whether the feature gate is enabled or not.

Thinking about this scenario:
1. Node is created but marked as unready. 
2. (1) arrives in the scheduler via EventHandler, but preCheck drops this event because of un-ready.
3. Node is now ready. 
4. (3) arrives in the scheduler via EventHandler, preCheck says OK this time.

For example, PodTopologySpread has NodeAdd and UpdateNodeLabel in EventsToHandler (before this PR). 
PodTopologySpread wants to requeue Pods at NodeAdd (2), but (2) doesn't arrive in the scheduling queue because of preCheck. And, because PodTopologySpread doesn't have NodeUpdate, (4) doesn't move Pods rejected by PodTopologySpread. This problematic scenario could happen regardless of the feature gate value.

OTOH, the existing functionality has been in production for a while, with no bug reports. So I wonder how commonly this happens?

Two requests:
1. Add integration tests to proof that this was a problem (specially around the NodeReady scenario).
2. Maybe we should consider targeting updates to NodeReady, as opposed to any update. Targeting any update has the potential of causing more regressions due to increased retries.

issue_context.title: plugins that register nodeAdd in EventsToRegister must register nodeUpdate
issue_context.body:
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign
/kind feature

Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.

---

Plugins may miss Node-related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

So, no matter whether plugins have QueueingHint or not, plugins must register NodeUpdate event when they're interested in NodeAdd. Also, in case they have QHint, they should take this scenario into consideration.

review_comments: Why is this specific to taints? what about a node that receives a node label update that impacts the nodeAffinity preCheck? Also, why doesn't the plugin explicitly add those instead of implicitly doing it here (which seems to me the right thing to do)?

cc @alculquicondor 

> what about a node that receives a node label update that impacts the nodeAffinity preCheck

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122292#issuecomment-1862867359 changed this PR's direction from adding a general node update to adding a node taint event.
You're actually right. If we want a complete fix (covering all minor scenarios), we should register `Node/Update` event here, but it'd hurt the throughput by requeueing many Pods unnecessarily.

So, the point would be which scenario(s) is likely enough to deserve a fix. And, I believe [this scenario](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122292#issuecomment-1861794637) is, while others aren't.

> we should register Node/Update event here, but it'd hurt the throughput by requeueing many Pods unnecessarily.

It could be a `UpdateNodeLabel`, not any update. But the next point is more important:

> So, the point would be which scenario(s) is likely enough to deserve a fix. And, I believe https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122292#issuecomment-1861794637 is, while others aren't.

Wouldn't in this scenario the taint/tolerations plugin be the one moving the unschedulable pods to the queue when the node update happens?

> Wouldn't in this scenario the taint/tolerations plugin be the one moving the unschedulable pods to the queue when the node update happens?

No, [in the example](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122292#issuecomment-1861794637), the Pod only has PodTopologySpread in unschedPlugin. So, the taint plugin doesn't move this Pod when the unready taint is removed. That's why we have to add `Node/UpdateTaint` event to PodTopologySpread plugin to let it move the Pod when taint is removed.

> It could be a UpdateNodeLabel, not any update.

Yeah, a smaller event may be enough for nodeaffinity case though, there are also other checks implemented in `preCheck` (node port and node allocatable resource). To cover all of them, we have to register Node/Update to notice a node port update, plus Pod/Delete as well? to catch an increase in allocatable resources in a Node.

Ok, I see. I think the right solution is to add the taint/toleration plugin to the list of UnschedulablePlugins for that pod when it fails preCheck on node add event. We could change the function signature of PreCheck to return the plugin that failed the pod.

The right solution is in the line of schedulingHints and the removal of prechecks.

But since we are not there yet, I'm ok with this incremental fix.

We are discussing the "right" solution for this PR. Since PreChecks continue to exist, then having them integrate with failedPlugins is certainly the better approach than this hack which could be surprising to plugins and is not really covering all corner cases.

I didn't get a chance to look at the implementation, but I didn't expect it to be that complicated.

Isn't the code behind `registerNodeAdded && !registerNodeTaintUpdated` below adding this automatically? Does it still make sense to also add this manually?

A short comment here that this is a workaround would be useful to avoid confusion when reading just this file, because nothing in it depends on node taints.

> Does it still make sense to also add this manually?

Yes, especially for QHint - When you add QHint for Node/Add, you probably want to have the same QHint for Node/UpdateNodeTaint, which you couldn't do if we let the scheduler automatically add `UpdateNodeTaint`.

> A short comment here that this is a workaround would be useful to avoid confusion when reading just this file, because nothing in it depends on node taints.

👍

> you probably want to have the same QHint for Node/UpdateNodeTaint,

This is the part that I don't get. This particular plugin doesn't check taints of a node. It leaves that to the other plugins which check whether a pod fits the node.

If you are adding it because "it might be needed", then it might be necessary. If it's getting added because "node added" is not delivered reliably (= i.e. it's a workaround), then it makes more sense.

It's not that "node added" events are not delivered reliably.

It's that a new node is likely not ready (it has a not-ready taint). And it needs to be retried when it becomes ready.
I am a little confused about this note. why do we have it here and in the other file too? It seems to be relevant only there.

Just for the visibility. The plugin developers would (hopefully) read this comment when they're using `Node` event. If we only write this comment in pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go, it'd be hidden behaviour for them.
Made it table-driven. It'll be the basis for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122305.
Let's open an issue for this. It should be possible to send a Broadcast to the sync.Cond in the queue.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123480
Can you revert this so that we don't depend on an owner for this file?

/approve

As test owner.

this is a more restrictive change, did we think carefully that limiting PodTopologySpread to label an taint updates is enough?

It should be OK. Actually before https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122195, we only has `UpdateNodeLabel` rather than `Update`. (was changed to `Update` to deal with [this issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284))
